reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) directly supports the formation of intergranular (Hf, Zr)B2 borides, enhanced grain-boundary cohesion, and improved ductility/work hardenability with minimal change in yield strength in the HfMoNbTaTiZr system. However, no evidence is provided for the retention of impact-induced energy release characteristics, which is a key premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Boron addition (≈0.1 at.%) to BCC RHEAs induces intergranular precipitation of (Hf, Zr)B2 borides
Intergranular borides enhance grain-boundary cohesion and change fracture mode from intergranular to transgranular
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion improves ductility and work hardenability without significantly altering matrix strength
The BCC matrix remains largely unaltered, preserving high strength
Impact-induced energy release characteristics are maintained because the bulk matrix is unchanged
